 32-Yr-Old HK Actress Marries Dad's Friend, 73, Who Is 10 Years Older Than Her 63-Yr-Old Father
 Cantonese opera actress Yemina Yu Chung Yan had known politician Lo Wai Kwok since primary school and called him “Uncle Lo” for more than 20 years.

 We've heard of couples with huge age gaps , but this one comes with quite the twist .
 Hong Kong Cantonese opera actress Yemina Yu Chung Yan, 32, recently tied the knot with 73-year-old politician Lo Wai Kwok, who is 41 years her senior.
 But here's the interesting part: He's a friend of her dad's and has known her since she was in primary school. She called him "Uncle Lo" for more than 20 years.
 Oh, and he's also 10 years older than her dad.
 The couple got married on October 11 at the Hong Kong Jockey Club's Beas River Country Club, with around 300 guests in attendance.
 Yemina later shared photos from their wedding on social media, including one of Wai Kwok serving tea to her 63-year-old father, veteran horse racing commentator Yu Pak Lok.
 The photo sparked discussion online, particularly because the groom is older than his father-in-law.
 Traditionally, newlyweds kneel when serving tea to their elders. However, the couple and Pak Lok remained standing throughout the ceremony.
 So how did "Uncle Lo" become her husband?
 It turns out Wai Kwok and Pak Lok became friends through their shared interests in horse racing and traditional arts more than two decades ago.
 Yemina was still a little girl then, having started learning Cantonese opera singing at five and performing on stage at six.
 Wai Kwok and his late wife, Wong Siu Chun, once attended a Cantonese opera competition where Yemina was performing.
 Impressed by her talent, Wai Kwok later discovered that the young performer was his friend's daughter.
 From then on, she addressed him as "Uncle Lo".
 The pair continued crossing paths at Cantonese opera events over the years.
 Around 2018, they even performed together in the Cantonese opera Lan Du Er Shu Lao Po ( 烂赌二赎老婆 ), in which Wai Kwok repeatedly called Yemina "wife".
 Who would have thought he'd eventually be calling her that in real life?
 Their relationship took a romantic turn in May this year, after Yemina completed her veterinary medicine final exams at City University of Hong Kong.
 The two started chatting over text about Cantonese opera and life, with their conversation lasting until the early hours of the morning.
 Yemina quoted a line from the Cantonese opera The Reincarnation of a Beauty ( 再世红梅记 ), to which Wai Kwok responded with another line expressing his admiration for her beauty and his wish to remain her lifelong companion.
 And things moved pretty quickly after that.
 Within just three weeks, they had decided to get married, booked their wedding venue, commissioned their rings and started preparing the wedding gown.
 Wai Kwok, who is chairman of Hong Kong's Business and Professionals Alliance, publicly introduced Yemina as his fiancée at a party meeting in May, before the couple announced their wedding plans to the media three days later.
 He is also a member of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) and a former Hong Kong legislator.
 His first wife, Wong Siu Chun, died of heart disease in August 2021. They had been together for more than 40 years and have a son. Wai Kwok also became a grandfather 16 years ago.
 Despite their 41-year age gap, the newlyweds have plenty in common, particularly their love for Cantonese opera, music and horses.
 Yemina, who graduated with first-class honours in veterinary medicine, was once the youngest Cantonese opera singing instructor at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts.
 Wai Kwok, meanwhile, studied Cantonese opera singing for seven years and plays several musical instruments.
 In a Facebook post, Wai Kwok revealed that they chose Beas River Country Club because of their shared love for horses. Yemina enjoys horse riding and previously interned at the Hong Kong Jockey Club.
 He also personally drove his prized red Ferrari 348 Spider to pick up his bride.
 Interestingly, the sports car was made in 1994 — the same year Yemina was born.
 Wai Kwok joked that it must be fate.
 At their wedding banquet, he showed off his musical talents by playing the saxophone and singing an English duet with his bride.
 As for what Yemina's dad thinks about his daughter marrying his longtime friend?
 Pak Lok reportedly said: "I have no problem with it."
 He described Wai Kwok as someone who values relationships and believes his daughter had thought carefully about her decision.
 The tea ceremony photo that got everyone talking.
 Wai Kwok picked up his bride in his red Ferrari, which was made in 1994, the same year Yemina was born.
 From "Uncle Lo" to hubby.
 The newlyweds have known each other for more than two decades.
 From playing husband and wife to becoming the real deal.
